issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]). In the provided solution, Bookstore defines init(books: [Book], valid: Bool) which adds an unexpected parameter. This also conflicts with the solution's Client usage which calls Bookstore(books: books) (no 'valid' argument). This mismatch will prevent compilation and confuses students about the required constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore initializer match the problem specification and the Client usage by removing the extra 'valid: Bool' parameter. Change the initializer to init(books: [Book]) and update its implementation accordingly (or, alternatively, update all call sites to provide the additional parameter consistently, but removing the extra parameter is the simpler fix to align with the exercise).

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]). The solution implementation introduces a different initializer signature init(books: [Book], valid: Bool), adding an extra parameter named 'valid'. This diverges from the API specified in the exercise and creates a mapping confusion for students who are asked to implement and use init(books:). The mismatch may lead students to implement the initializer as specified in the problem but find a conflicting signature in the provided solution, increasing extraneous cognitive load about which initializer is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Bookstore initializer with the problem statement. Either remove the extra 'valid' parameter from the solution initializer so it becomes init(books: [Book]), or provide a default value for the new parameter (e.g. valid: Bool = true) and document it, so calls using only books: remain valid. The preferred fix is to match the required signature: init(books: [Book]).
